paper_metadata.title: Surgical Outcome in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: A Multicenter Survey

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a multicenter consecutive series, which is strong, but the recruitment period is extremely long (1950-2003), introducing significant historical bias in surgical techniques and diagnostic standards. Participation rates of eligible vs. non-eligible patients are not reported.

items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The study population comprised 70 TSC patients who underwent surgery for refractory epilepsy.
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined as patients with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) undergoing epilepsy surgery across multiple named centers.

items.evidence_snippet: Subjects consisted of a consecutive series of patients who underwent preoperative assessment and surgery
items.reasoning: While 'consecutive' is stated, the referral patterns and specific screening processes at each of the diverse international centers are not detailed.

items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly provided, though the inclusion of a 1950 patient is a significant outlier.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While definitions are provided, the multicenter retrospective nature over 50 years means that measurement of factors like 'mental retardation' and 'EEG focality' likely varied significantly in criteria and technology (e.g., MRI strength).

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The association between outcome and the following variables was examined: sex; age of seizure onset; age at TSC diagnosis; presence/prior history of infantile spasms; the presence or absence of mental retardation; number of cortical tubers; ictal and interictal focality...
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly listed and categorized.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Only MRI and EEG data were consistently reported among all centers, and were considered in the analysis.
items.reasoning: Standard clinical tools (MRI/EEG) were used, but reliability across centers and across decades (1950s vs 2000s) is highly questionable.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Interval data were also divided into groups (defined in Table 2) so that all variables could be subjected to the same analyses.
items.reasoning: Cut-points like '12 months' for seizure onset are used; it is unclear if these were pre-specified or determined post-hoc based on the data distribution.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Methods taken by each center to isolate the dominant epileptogenic tuber were widely variable
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly admit that methods were variable across the different centers.

items.evidence_snippet: Age at seizure onset (n = 69)... Number of cortical tubers (n = 53)
items.reasoning: Some variables have near-complete data (69/70), but others like tuber count (53/70) have significant missingness (24%).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The Engel Class is a validated, standard tool for epilepsy surgery outcomes, and the follow-up time is reported, though the retrospective nature means assessment was not blinded to prognostic factors.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Surgical outcome was defined as Engel Class I-IV (Engel et al., 1993)... Time from surgery to evaluation (n = 70) 5.2 (8.0) [years]
items.reasoning: The Engel classification is a standard metric, and follow-up duration is provided.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Surgical outcome was defined as Engel Class I-IV
items.reasoning: Engel Class is reliable, but there is no mention of blinding the outcome assessors to the prognostic factors (e.g., MRI findings).

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Surgical outcome was defined as Engel Class I-IV (Engel et al., 1993) for correlation and regression analyses.
items.reasoning: The same classification system was applied to all patients across centers.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable regression to account for confounding, which is a strength. However, the 'residual tuber' finding was counter-intuitive, and the authors acknowledge that surgical approach (a major confounder) varied and was not fully controlled.

items.evidence_snippet: The association between outcome and the following variables was examined: sex; age of seizure onset... number of surgical stages, extent of surgical procedure...
items.reasoning: Key clinical variables are measured, but specific AED (medication) changes and surgical technique variations over 50 years are not fully captured.

items.evidence_snippet: Single-stage surgery was a resection in one operative procedure. Two-stage surgery was an intracranial EEG study followed by resection.
items.reasoning: Surgical stages and procedures are defined.
